Third, Owen — the carrier's written consent requirement before seeking injunctive relief is a prerequisite we cannot ignore. Filing without it could jeopardize our coverage. We need to obtain that consent before any filing decision is signed.

Based on all three reports, here's where I think we stand: We cannot authorize filing today as-is. We have three prerequisites that must be completed first — (1) updating the strategy memorandum to reflect the Cook County forum clause, (2) updating the evidence chart to accurately reflect that only customer-list database copying is forensically supported, and (3) obtaining the carrier's prior written consent before seeking injunctive relief. Once those three items are addressed, I can record authorization subject to those stated prerequisites being completed. Does anyone have any concerns with this approach, or am I missing anything else material?
